deep.reconstruction:
This is a printed page (p. 59) of an elementary German arithmetic textbook. It belongs to the section on compound proportion and the chain rule ('Kettenregel', 'Wechsel-Arbitragen'). It sits in a bound volume whose interleaved or facing pages carry Gauss's notes. The left-margin fragments ('+ &c', '(1-g sin…)^-μ', '(1+g sin…)', '…¾k)') are the cut-off edge of Gauss's handwritten series and quadrature formulas on the facing page (the previous page). They are not related to the printed text.

(1) End of an earlier conversion problem, recast as a compound proportion.
- First link: 6:5 = 3 fl : y fl.
- Second link: 63:34 = y : x (fl to rthl).
- Multiplying the proportions termwise gives (6·63):(5·34) = 3 fl : x rthl.
- Hence x = 5·34·3/(6·63) rthl. My evaluation: 510/378 = 85/63 ≈ 1.349 rthl.

(2) Converting 723 ducats into Hamburg Banco-thalers.
- Data: 1 ducat = 7 mk 2 schilling Courant. With 16 schilling = 1 mark (my note), this is 7⅛ mk, so 8 duc = 57 mk Cour.
- Agio of Banco over Courant is 18¾ %: 118¾ mk Cour = 100 mk Banco, i.e. 475 mk Cour = 400 mk Bco.
- 3 mk Bco = 1 rthl Bco.
- Chain rule: x rthl Bco = 723 duc · (57/8) · (400/475) · (1/3) = 723·57·400/(8·475·3).
- The same computation is restated as three chained proportions with intermediates z (mk Cour) and y (mk Bco). Multiplying them gives the same formula.
- Result: since 57·400 = 22800 = 2·(8·475·3), x = 723·2 = 1446 rthl Bco.

(3) Statement only; the solution is on the next page.
- Data: ducat valued at 2 rthl Banco, ¼ % better than Banco, so 50 duc = 100¼ rthl Bco, i.e. 200 duc = 401 rthl Bco.
- Louis d'or = 10 mk 13½ sch = 173½ sch Banco, so 2 Ld'or = 347 sch Bco.
- Question: by what percent does the ducat valued at 2¾ rthl light money differ from the Louis d'or valued at 5 rthl light money?
- Method: find the value of 100 rthl (ducat-money at 2¾) in Louis d'or-money. The page ends with the beginning of the chain, 'x rthl.'
- Completion (from the next page): x = 100·4·401·48·2·5/(11·200·347) = 384960/3817 ≈ 100.854, using 1 rthl Bco = 48 sch. So the difference is about 0.854 %.
errors: Minor typographic omission in the original: the second proportion in problem 2 lacks a colon ('z mk. C. y mk. Bco.' should read 'z mk. C. : y mk. Bco.').
